title: This Worm Shoots Glue From Its Head, Then Eats the Glue
subject: velvet worm

scenes.text: This worm shoots glue from its head. Then it eats the glue.
The velvet worm waits in the dark. When a cricket walks by, it fires slime at three to five meters per second.
The slime fans out in every direction, from nozzles only fifty to two hundred microns wide.
The jets make a sticky net. The more the prey struggles, the more tangled it gets.
Then the worm bites it and liquefies it with digestive juices.
The slime is expensive. It takes about three weeks to make more, so the worm eats the leftovers.
